claims.quote: Gallego [arxiv_2209.12330] proposes aesthetic gradients, a method that guides a CLIP-conditioned diffusion model toward custom visual aesthetics derived from a user-supplied set of images.

Avrahami et al. [arxiv_2211.14305] observe that despite the impressive quality of text-to-image diffusion models, fine-grained control over the shapes and layout of individual regions remains elusive, particularly because prior approaches relied on fixed label sets.

Zhong et al. [arxiv_2305.05189] address a different bottleneck—semantic understanding—by augmenting pre-trained diffusion models with large language models via a SUR-adapter, improving commonsense reasoning when input prompts are concise or narrative in nature.

Concept ablation techniques [arxiv_2303.13516] extend controllability in the opposite direction, enabling selective removal of specific styles or memorized identities from pre-trained models without full retraining—an important capability for responsible deployment.

Early text-to-image diffusion models established strong baselines for photorealistic synthesis by leveraging web-scale paired datasets, yet persistent challenges remained in achieving reliable text-image correspondence, particularly in domain-specific settings [arxiv_2308.08157].

The challenge of multi-prompt spatial guidance has also been addressed through differentiable optimal transport, enabling simultaneous conditioning on multiple textual cues to steer generation toward compositionally complex targets [arxiv_2204.08472].

InstructPix2Pix demonstrated that combining a large language model with a text-to-image model to synthesize paired training data allows a single network to follow free-form human editing instructions at inference time [arxiv_2211.09800].

X-IQE proposes an explainable quality assessment framework using visual large language models and hierarchical chain-of-thought reasoning to produce human-aligned textual judgements of generated images [arxiv_2305.10843], offering a more interpretable alternative to scalar metrics for benchmarking both generation and editing systems.

One foundational approach involves learning efficient noise schedules rather than relying on fixed, hand-crafted ones. Watson et al. [arxiv_2106.03802] demonstrated that the discrete-time step sequence used during sampling can be optimized directly, enabling high-quality generation with far fewer denoising steps.

At the systems level, ReDi [arxiv_2302.02285] introduces a learning-free retrieval-based framework that shortens diffusion trajectories by retrieving precomputed intermediate states, while post-training quantization [arxiv_2305.10657] reduces model size and latency without retraining.

FateZero [arxiv_2303.09535] achieves zero-shot text-based video editing by fusing cross-frame attentions without per-prompt training, demonstrating that inversion-based editing principles transfer beyond static images.

The tendency of diffusion models to memorise training data [arxiv_2305.20086] raises additional concerns about replication of copyrighted content, motivating concept ablation techniques [arxiv_2303.13516] that selectively remove specific styles or identities from pre-trained models without full retraining.
